highlights.title: Trio 1.0.0 major release
changes: Dosing algorithm moved from JavaScript to native Swift, so calculations are faster and use less battery.
Supports Omnipod 5, FreeStyle Libre 3/3+ (Beta), Eversense E3/365, and Accu-Chek SmartGuide CGMs.
Home screen and chart were rebuilt to let you drag, pinch and scrub up to 72 hours of data.
Alarms, watch and lock-screen forecasts, dosing modes, Quick-Pick treatments, and accessibility were improved.

highlights.title: Dosing Mode replaces Closed Loop toggle
changes: The Closed Loop toggle in Settings is replaced by a Dosing Mode picker.
Only Closed and Open modes are offered in Settings right now, with short explanatory hints.
Your existing Closed Loop setting is migrated automatically: true → Closed, false → Open, unknown → Open.
The Manual Temp Basal screen and related controls have been removed.
Onboarding now pre-fills Max IOB to one third of your total daily basal instead of leaving it at zero.

highlights.title: Add Low Glucose Suspend and Basal Testing modes
changes: Adds two new dosing modes: Low Glucose Suspend and Basal Testing.
Low Glucose Suspend treats your Max IOB as 0 so Trio will not add corrective insulin.
Basal Testing fixes sensitivity and disables dynamic ISF so you can observe your programmed basals, and only suspends <.
Entering Basal Testing cancels any Trio-set temp basal and Trio will otherwise recommend no temp basals.
These modes are temporary overrides that do not modify your saved preferences, so your settings are restored when you退出.

highlights.title: Loop pill shows open-loop state and device health
changes: The loop pill no longer claims to be looping when Trio is in open loop.
In open loop the ring reports device health: green while CGM and pump report, red on device issues.
The time caption is shown only in closed loop and is hidden in open loop to avoid implying an action.
The loop icon is now an open ring with horizontal gaps and a centre symbol for constrained modes, and it scales with a�.
Pull-to-refresh can no longer force a loop when Trio is in open loop.

highlights.title: Show algorithm's open-loop bolus suggestion
changes: The bolus screen now shows the algorithm's open-loop bolus suggestion.
That suggested amount is reduced by your Recommended Bolus Percentage and capped by Max Bolus.
The suggestion is hidden when the algorithm asks for a basal reduction instead of a bolus.
Open loop still does not deliver the suggested bolus; this only displays the recommendation.

items.title: Prevent launch crash by delaying telemetry startup
changes: Trio no longer crashes on simulator or debug launches caused by telemetry starting too early.
Telemetry now starts only after the Core Data persistent stores finish loading.
Foreground-transition telemetry checks do nothing until telemetry has been initialized.
Cold-launch telemetry timestamps are recorded about one second later than before.
A remaining race on push-notification cold-launches was left for a follow-up.

includedPullRequests.body:
Open loop computes `insulinReq` every cycle and never enacts it, and nothing surfaced it.

includedPullRequests.body:
## Summary 
This PR moves the six reviewed parts (#1504, #1505, #1506, #1507, #1508 and #1509) into dev. Each was reviewed and merged individually; this is the integration PR.

It replaces the **Closed Loop toggle** with a Dosing Mode picker: Closed Loop, Open Loop, Low Glucose Suspend, Basal Testing. Each mode carries an AutomationLevel, `off` / `hypoSuspendOnly` / `reductionsOnly` / `full` (i.e. closed-loop).

  - Open Loop is now a "real mode": Trio surfaces forecasts, COB and IOB update properly, treatment view is fully functional. Closes #643.
  - Low Glucose Suspend: Trio may only lower or stop basal, never correct a high. See also: https://androidaps.readthedocs.io/en/3.1/Configuration/Config-Builder.html#low-glucose-suspend-lgs
  - Basal Testing: Trio does no adjustment at all unless glucose actually goes low, with sensitivity adaptation pinned so the user can actually measure their basal profile.

The constrained modes work by clamping the algorithm's inputs, not the user's settings. Stored preferences always remain unchanged, so switching back restores everything and manual bolusing keeps honoring real Max IOB. Verified on real device(s) during testing.

 Closes #644.

includedPullRequests.title: Fix launch crash: start telemetry after Core Data initialization
includedPullRequests.body:
## Problem

Debug/simulator launches of current dev crash within seconds:

```
NSInternalInconsistencyException: This NSPersistentStoreCoordinator has no persistent stores (unknown). It cannot perform a save operation.
```

Crashing queues are `NSManagedObjectContext: storeGlucose` and `storeBatteryStatus`.

## Cause

Since #1367, `TelemetryClient.shared` resolves through the DI container with eager `injectServices`. `AppDelegate.didFinishLaunchingWithOptions` calls it at launch, which resolves `APSManager` + `FetchGlucoseManager` and thereby constructs `BaseDeviceDataManager` — the whole APS/device graph — **before** `CoreDataStack.initializeStack()` has finished loading the persistent stores.

The CGM and pump **simulators** deliver status/readings immediately on construction, so their first Core Data save races the store load and aborts the app. Real hardware usually wins the race (BLE reconnect latency), which is why reports cluster on simulator-configured dev setups; a Debug/TSAN build widens the window further. The launch-order log signature: a healthy launch logs `Successfully loaded persistent store` *before* `PumpManagerState` is persisted; a crashing one persists `PumpManagerState` immediately and never reaches the store-load line.

## Fix

`AppDelegate` no longer resolves services at launch (only the Crashlytics gate remains, which touches plists only). Telemetry starts at the end of `TrioApp.loadServices()` — i.e. strictly after Core Data initialization — with the identical cadence sequence as before (install ID, cold-launch recording, SHA-change ping, recurring timer, overdue check). The foreground-transition hook receives its `TelemetryClient` reference from `loadServices()` and no-ops before that.

This deliberately does **not** reintroduce the old `injectIfNeeded` deferral; eager injection stays, only the call site moves behind the initialization barrier.

## Notes

- Cold-launch timestamps are now recorded ~1 s later (post store load) — immaterial to the 7-day sliding window.
- A latent same-class race remains on the APNS path (`TrioRemoteControl.shared` in `didReceiveRemoteNotification` when a push cold-launches the app). It predates #1367 and is left for a follow-up.

includedPullRequests.title: MAJOR RELEASE Trio v1.0.0
includedPullRequests.body:
For detailed release notes, see: https://github.com/nightscout/Trio/releases/tag/v1.0

## What's Changed At A Glance

- **Trio thinks in your iPhone's "own language" now** – the dosing algorithm was rewritten from JavaScript into native Swift; identical decisions, twice as fast, easier on your battery
- **Omnipod 5** – full support, including the guided first-pod setup (requires one-time internet connection)
- **FreeStyle Libre 3 and 3+ (Beta)** – paired directly in Trio, with no companion app and no internet connection needed to loop
- **Eversense E3 and 365** – the implanted sensor family, with optional upload to Eversense DMS
- **Accu-Chek SmartGuide** – Roche's 14-day sensor, now a first-class Trio CGM
- **A rebuilt Home screen** – drag, pinch and scrub through up to 72 hours of data in Trio's chart, with one smart panel that surfaces whatever needs your attention
- **A Modernized Look** – Liquid Glass has made its way to Trio, making it look like a proper iOS 26+ app
- **Alarms you can actually hear** – four separate bugs were silencing them; on iOS 26 and later, critical alarms now sound even when iOS has put Trio to sleep
- **Dosing Modes** – the Closed Loop switch becomes a four-way choice: Closed Loop, Open Loop, Low Glucose Suspend and Basal Testing
- **Quick-Pick Treatments** – Trio learns the amounts you actually use and puts them one tap away
- **Forecasts on your wrist and lock screen** – the glucose prediction now appears on the Apple Watch app and in the Live Activity
- **Garmin complications** – put glucose, IOB and COB on any Connect IQ watch face
- **Built for everyone** – massively improved accessibility pass across VoiceOver, Dynamic Type and contrast
- **Release notes inside the app** – read what changed without leaving Trio
- **Steadier under the hood** – a large reliability pass on data storage, background work and pump event handling
- **Anonymous diagnostics are on by default** – no health data is ever sent, and opting out is one tap in Settings

includedPullRequests.body:
For detailed release notes, see: https://github.com/nightscout/Trio/releases/tag/v1.0

## What's Changed At A Glance

- **Trio thinks in your iPhone's "own language" now** – the dosing algorithm was rewritten from JavaScript into native Swift; identical decisions, twice as fast, easier on your battery
- **Omnipod 5** – full support, including the guided first-pod setup (requires one-time internet connection)
- **FreeStyle Libre 3 and 3+ (Beta)** – paired directly in Trio, with no companion app and no internet connection needed to loop
- **Eversense E3 and 365** – the implanted sensor family, with optional upload to Eversense DMS
- **Accu-Chek SmartGuide** – Roche's 14-day sensor, now a first-class Trio CGM
- **A rebuilt Home screen** – drag, pinch and scrub through up to 72 hours of data in Trio's chart, with one smart panel that surfaces whatever needs your attention
- **A Modernized Look** – Liquid Glass has made its way to Trio, making it look like a proper iOS 26+ app
- **Alarms you can actually hear** – four separate bugs were silencing them; on iOS 26 and later, critical alarms now sound even when iOS has put Trio to sleep
- **Dosing Modes** – the Closed Loop switch becomes a four-way choice: Closed Loop, Open Loop, Low Glucose Suspend and Basal Testing
- **Quick-Pick Treatments** – Trio learns the amounts you actually use and puts them one tap away
- **Forecasts on your wrist and lock screen** – the glucose prediction now appears on the Apple Watch app and in the Live Activity
- **Garmin complications** – put glucose, IOB and COB on any Connect IQ watch face
- **Built for everyone** – massively improved accessibility pass across VoiceOver, Dynamic Type and contrast
- **Release notes inside the app** – read what changed without leaving Trio
- **Steadier under the hood** – a large reliability pass on data storage, background work and pump event handling
- **Anonymous diagnostics are on by default** – no health data is ever sent, and opting out is one tap in Settings
